result.summary:
Wrote docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md: the T-24h 'Still coming?' reconfirmation job and the T-3h route+QR reminder job, both going through REQ-025's sendLedgeredNotification ledger.

REQ-011 AGENDA SHAPE CONFIRMED SUFFICIENT -- NOT A BLOCKER (Sec0): apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts's AgendaItem is {kind: string; at: string; label: string}, and a doors item is identified as the element whose kind === 'doors' -- the exact same check validateAgenda (REQ-016, already implemented) uses for its 'at most one doors item' and 'doors not after starts_at' rules, and the exact same check REQ-011's own proven jsonb_path_query_first SQL query performs. This design reuses that identification directly (a new findDoorsAgendaItem(agenda): AgendaItem | null in event.ts, signature only, rule stated as a table, no body) -- no competing convention invented.

SCHEMA CHANGE -- NO, confirmed by direct inspection, so DATA-DESIGNER does NOT run this cycle (WF-02 Step 0.9 only calls it in when stored data changes): registrations.reconfirmed_at ALREADY EXISTS (schema.ts line 261, added by REQ-011, unused until now -- REQ-026 is simply its first writer). notification_ledger already exists (REQ-025); REQ-026 only adds two NotificationKind TypeScript union members ('reminder_24h', 'reminder_3h') already anticipated by name in REQ-025's own design and by the ledger's deliberately-text (not pgEnum) kind column -- a one-line type change, not a migration. No doors_at column is added anywhere (decisions/0007, binding).

GAP FOUND AND CLOSED IN REQ-025'S SEND API (Sec1): NotificationSender.send(tgId, text) is text-only -- no inline keyboard, no photo. T-24h needs two buttons; T-3h needs a QR photo with caption. Rather than build a second, parallel send path (which would violate 'reuse sendLedgeredNotification, don't reimplement'), the design EXTENDS REQ-025's already-built domain/notification.ts and scheduler/rateLimiter.ts: composeMessage's return type becomes a closed ComposedMessage union (text+buttons / photo+caption / skip), NotificationSender gains sendPhoto and an optional buttons param on send, SendOutcome gains 'skipped-stale'. sendLedgeredNotification's steps 1-4 (ledger insert, blocked/broadcast checks) are UNCHANGED -- only step 5 branches on the composed result's kind. The one existing caller (handlers/withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification) needs a one-line wrapper-shape migration (bare string -> {kind:'text', text}), stated precisely in Sec1.4, plus an export keyword so REQ-026's decline handler can reuse it directly (Sec7.2) instead of duplicating the promotion-notification composition.

AT-SEND-TIME RECHECK (Sec2, Sec5.1/5.2 step 1-3): a new getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent(db, registrationId) read, called inside each job's composeMessage closure (which sendLedgeredNotification invokes AFTER the ledger insert commits, per REQ-025's own step ordering) -- withdrawn-since-selection or event-no-longer-published both return {kind:'skip'}, which sendLedgeredNotification surfaces as 'skipped-stale' with NO sender call, while the already-committed ledger row is deliberately left in place (same accepted under-sending-only risk REQ-025 Sec3.2 already names, extended to the skip case).

DOORS-TIME BYTE-FOR-BYTE REUSE (Sec5.2 step 4, AC7): the T-3h caption's doors line calls formatDateTimeInTimezone(new Date(doorsItem.at), event.chapterTimezone, lang) -- stated explicitly as the SAME function, same three arguments in the same order as buildEventCardContent's agendaLines mapping (REQ-017, domain/event.ts) already applies to that same AgendaItem. This is what makes AC7 hold structurally, not by coincidence of two independently-written format calls agreeing.

RECONFIRM DOMAIN LOGIC (Sec4): decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration added to domain/registration.ts, mirroring decideWithdrawOutcome/withdrawRegistration's exact existing shape (pure decision + SELECT-FOR-UPDATE transactional write). reconfirmRegistration's UPDATE touches ONLY reconfirmed_at -- admission is never in its SET clause, which is what makes AC2's 'admission UNCHANGED' true structurally.

DECLINE REUSES withdrawRegistration UNCHANGED (Sec7.2): the T-24h 'Can't make it' callback calls domain/registration.ts's existing withdrawRegistration exactly as handlers/withdraw.ts's own confirm handler does, including the identical post-commit sendPromotionNotification call on a promotion -- no reimplementation of withdrawal or auto-promotion logic anywhere in this design.

INDEX.TS SEQUENCING FIX FLAGGED PRECISELY (Sec8): today's index.ts calls startScheduledJobs([]) immediately after `new Bot(...)`, before bot.start() -- fine only because REQ-025 passes an empty job list. REQ-026's T-3h job needs botUsername (for renderCheckInQrPng) but has no ctx to read it from (unlike handlers/my.ts's ctx.me.username). Design requires index.ts to `await bot.init()` (populates bot.botInfo without blocking on bot.start()'s never-resolving long-poll promise) before startScheduledJobs(...), read botUsername = bot.botInfo.username once, and thread it into makeReminder3hJob -- stated as an explicit, mechanical index.ts change, not left for BACKEND-DEV to discover via a runtime failure.

Every one of the 10 ACs mapped to a concrete design element in Sec10's table. 3 open questions stated explicitly (Sec9): the ledger-key-reuse-across-a-withdraw-then-re-register-cycle limitation (structurally identical to REQ-025's own Sec8 open question 2, left unsolved for the same reason -- no AC exercises it), whether sendPhoto should share send's rate-limit window (yes, stated as a deliberate choice, not exercised by any AC), and the failed-T-3h-send-after-ledger-commit risk (restates REQ-025 Sec3.2's accepted risk for the photo path).
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 1b) -- DATA-DESIGNER does not run this cycle, no stored-data change (registrations.reconfirmed_at and notification_ledger both already exist; only a TypeScript union extension is needed).
